column2: 由 rub（擦）＋ -er 构成；「橡胶」一义源自它能当擦子用，取代了早先的 caoutchouc
column3: an elastic material that stretches and springs back
column5: The tyres are made of hard rubber.|She erased the line with a rubber.
column6: the stuff that rubs marks away and springs back – 能擦掉痕迹又弹回原形的材料
column7: 橡胶：有弹性的工业材料|橡皮：用来擦掉铅笔痕的小块

column2: 中古英语 robous（废料、碎砖），更早词源不明；或与盎格鲁诺曼语 rubous 有关
column3: waste material to be thrown away, or nonsense
column5: They put the rubbish out on Tuesday.|He dismissed the claim as rubbish.
column6: what is thrown out as worthless – 当作无用而丢出去的东西
column7: 垃圾：丢弃的废弃物|废话：毫无价值的言论

column2: 中古英语 rumour ← 古法语 rumeur ← 拉丁语 rūmor（众口相传）
column3: a story passed between people without proof
column5: A rumor spread through the office quickly.|Do not repeat that rumor.
column6: common talk passed from mouth to mouth – 众口相传而未经证实的话
column7: 谣言：无根据且多为不实的传言|传闻：辗转听来的说法

column2: 中古英语 sacred，为 sacren（使成圣）的过去分词；sacre ← 古法语 sacrer ← 拉丁语 sacrāre（奉为神圣）
column3: connected with a god and treated with great respect
column5: This grove is sacred to the villagers.|They sang sacred music that evening.
column6: set apart and given over to a god – 分出来奉给神的
column7: 神圣的：不可侵犯、须敬重的|宗教的：与教门仪典有关的

column2: 中古英语 sacrifice ← 古法语 sacrifice ← 拉丁语 sacrificium，由 sacrum（圣物）＋ facere（做）构成
column3: something given up for a purpose, or to give it up
column5: She made real sacrifices for her family.|They sacrificed a lamb at dawn.
column6: making something over to a higher end – 把东西交出去成就更高的目的
column7: 牺牲：为某目的而舍弃所重视的|祭品：献给神的那件东西

column2: 古英语 sadol ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sadul ← 原始日耳曼语 *sadulaz，更早或与 *sed-（坐）有关
column3: a seat fastened on the back of a horse or bicycle
column5: He tightened the saddle before mounting.|The saddle needs new leather.
column6: a seat strapped on for riding – 绑上去供人骑坐的座具

column2: 古英语 seġl ← 原始西日耳曼语 *segl ← 原始日耳曼语 *seglą
column3: a large sheet of cloth that catches wind to move a boat
column5: The wind filled the white sail.|They sailed south for three days.
column6: cloth spread to catch the wind – 张开来受风的布
column7: 帆：船上受风的布篷|航行：靠船在水上行进

column2: 早期 sailer 的变体 ← 中古英语 sailer，由 sail ＋ -or 构成
column3: a person who works on a ship
column5: The sailor coiled the heavy rope.|Two sailors stayed aboard overnight.
column6: one whose work is sailing – 以行船为业的人
column7: 海员：在海船上工作的人|船员：船上任职的成员

column2: 中古英语 saint ← 古法语 saint（并与古英语 sanct 合流）← 拉丁语 sānctus（受奉为圣的），为 sancīre（使神圣）的过去分词
column3: a person recognized by a church as very holy
column5: The church is named after a saint.|Pilgrims prayed before the saint image.
column6: one set apart as holy – 被分出来称为圣的人
column7: 圣人：德行极高受尊崇的人|圣徒：教会正式册封的圣者

column2: 古英语 sacu（讼争、事由）← 原始西日耳曼语 *saku ← 原始日耳曼语 *sakō（事端、指控）
column3: the purpose or benefit for which something is done
column5: He agreed for the sake of peace.|Do it for your own sake.
column6: the cause on whose account one acts – 据以行事的那个由头
column7: 缘故：做某事所据的理由|利益：所要顾及的好处

column2: 中古英语 salade ← 古法语 salade ← 北意大利语 salada ← 俗拉丁语 *salāta，源自拉丁语 sal（盐）；罗马时代的菜蔬以盐水或油醋调味
column3: a cold dish of raw vegetables mixed together
column5: She made a salad with fresh leaves.|The salad came with warm bread.
column6: greens dressed with salt and oil – 用盐与油醋拌过的生菜
column7: 色拉：生菜拌调味汁的冷盘|凉拌菜：不加热拌成的菜

column2: 中古英语 salarie ← 古法语 salaire ← 拉丁语 salārium（工钱），为形容词 salārius（与盐有关的）的中性形，源自 sal（盐）
column3: a fixed amount of money paid regularly for work
column5: Her salary rose by five percent.|They pay the salary on the last day.
column6: the regular payment once reckoned in salt – 定期支付的报酬，早先与盐相关
column7: 薪水：按月领取的固定报酬|工资：为劳动所得的报酬

column2: 古英语 sala（卖出）← 古诺尔斯语 sala ← 原始日耳曼语 *salō（交付）
column3: the act of selling something, or a period of reduced prices
column5: The sale of the house took months.|Winter coats are on sale now.
column6: handing goods over for money – 把货交出去换钱
column7: 出售：把东西卖出去|减价：降价促销的时段

column2: 由 sales ＋ man 构成
column3: a man whose job is selling goods
column5: The salesman explained each model carefully.|A salesman called about insurance.
column6: the man who does the selling – 专管卖货的人
column7: 售货员：在店里卖货的人|推销员：上门或外出促销的人

column2: 古英语 sealt ← 原始西日耳曼语 *salt ← 原始日耳曼语 *saltą ← 原始印欧语 *sḗh₂l
column3: a white substance used to season and preserve food
column5: Add a little salt to the water.|Salt was once traded like money.
column6: the white grain that seasons and keeps food – 用来调味并保存食物的白色颗粒

column2: 中古英语 same ← 古诺尔斯语 samr 与古英语 same，同出原始日耳曼语 *samaz
column3: not different from another thing or person
column5: They arrived on the same train.|Both cups have the same shape.
column6: not differing from the other – 与另一个没有分别
column7: 相同的：彼此之间没有差别|同一的：指的就是那一个

column2: 中古英语 saumple ← 古法语 essample（例子）← 拉丁语 exemplum
column3: a small part taken to show what the whole is like
column5: They tested a sample from each batch.|The survey sampled two hundred households.
column6: a small part standing for the whole – 取一小份代表整体
column7: 样品：取出供检验或展示的一件|抽样：从整体中抽取部分来考察

column2: 中古法语 sanction ← 拉丁语 sānctiō（确立、制裁），源自 sancīre（使有效）
column3: official permission, or a penalty imposed on a country
column5: The plan needs official sanction first.|Trade sanctions hurt both sides.
column6: making something binding, whether by allowing or punishing – 使某事具有约束力，或准或罚
column7: 认可：正式许可使其有效|制裁：施加惩罚性措施

column2: 古英语 sand ← 原始西日耳曼语 *samd ← 原始日耳曼语 *samdaz
column3: tiny loose grains of worn rock found on beaches
column5: Sand filled his shoes at the beach.|Waves smoothed the wet sand.
column6: rock worn down into loose grains – 岩石磨成的松散颗粒

column2: 取自据传的发明者 Sandwich 伯爵之名
column3: two slices of bread with a filling between them
column5: He packed a sandwich for the trip.|She cut the sandwich in half.
column6: a filling held between two slices – 夹在两片之间的一份吃食

column2: 借自拉丁语 sānus（健全的）
column3: having a healthy mind, or showing good judgment
column5: The doctor found him entirely sane.|That was the only sane choice.
column6: sound in mind – 心智健全的
column7: 神志正常的：精神健全没有失常|明智的：判断稳妥合理

column2: 由 sarcasm ＋ -astic 构成，或借自法语 sarcastique ← 晚期拉丁语 sarcasmus ← 希腊语 sarkasmos，源自 sarx（肉）
column3: saying the opposite of what is meant in order to mock
column5: His sarcastic reply annoyed everyone.|She made a sarcastic remark about it.
column6: words that tear at someone under a smile – 笑着说出的、割人的话
column7: 讽刺的：反话相讥|尖刻的：言辞锋利伤人

column2: 中古法语 satellite ← 拉丁语 satelles（侍从），更早或出伊特鲁里亚语
column3: an object that moves around a planet, natural or man-made
column5: The satellite circles the earth twice daily.|A satellite relays the signal.
column6: an attendant body kept in orbit around another – 随行绕另一物运转的天体

column2: 中古法语 satire ← 拉丁语 satira，更早作 satura，出自 lanx satura（满盘杂陈）
column3: writing that uses humour to expose faults
column5: The play is a sharp satire.|His column relies on satire.
column6: a mixed dish of mockery served up – 杂陈成盘的嘲弄
column7: 讽刺作品：以嘲弄揭露弊病的作品|讥讽：出言挖苦

column2: 中古英语 sauce ← 古法语 sause ← 俗拉丁语 *salsa，为拉丁语 salsus（加了盐的）的阴性名词化，源自 sal（盐）
column3: a thick liquid served with food to add flavour
column5: Pour the sauce over the noodles.|This sauce contains no dairy.
column6: a salted liquid poured over food – 淋在食物上的加味液体
column7: 酱汁：浓稠的佐餐液体|调味汁：用来加味的汁水

column2: 中古英语 saucer ← 古法语 saussier（盛酱器）
column3: a small shallow dish that a cup stands on
column5: She set the cup on its saucer.|A saucer caught the spilled tea.
column6: the little dish that once held sauce – 早先用来盛酱的小盘
column7: 茶碟：垫在茶杯下的小盘|托碟：承托杯具的浅盘

column2: 中古英语 sawsiche ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 sausiche ← 晚期拉丁语 salsīcia，为 salsīcius（用盐调味的）的阴性形，源自拉丁语 salsus（加盐的）
column3: chopped meat packed into a thin tube of skin
column5: He fried two sausages for breakfast.|The sausage split while cooking.
column6: salted meat packed into a casing – 用盐调味后灌进肠衣的肉

column2: 中古英语 savage ← 古法语 sauvage（野生的）← 晚期拉丁语 salvāticus，为拉丁语 silvāticus（林中的）的变体，源自 silva（森林）
column3: fierce and violent, or very harsh
column5: The dog gave a savage bark.|Critics were savage about the film.
column6: wild as something out of the woods – 像林中之物那样未经驯服
column7: 野蛮的：粗野残酷不讲情理|凶猛的：攻击性强而猛烈

column2: 古英语 saga／sagu（锯）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sagu ← 原始日耳曼语 *sagô ← 原始印欧语 *sek-（切）
column3: a tool with a toothed blade for cutting wood
column5: He cut the plank with a saw.|They sawed the branch into logs.
column6: a toothed blade that cuts by drawing back and forth – 靠来回拉动切割的齿刃
column7: 锯：带齿的切割工具|锯开：用锯把东西切断

column2: 古英语 seċġan ← 原始西日耳曼语 *saggjan ← 原始日耳曼语 *sagjaną
column3: to speak words aloud
column5: She said nothing for a while.|He says the same thing daily.
column6: putting thought out in spoken words – 把想法用话说出去
column7: 说：把话讲出来|讲述：把事情叙说一遍
